title: Proactive Early Decannulation in Neurological Early Rehabilitation: A Multicenter Randomized Controlled Trial with Parallel-Group Design
summary:
This study tests whether a clear, criteria‑based plan for early removal of the tracheostomy tube (early decannulation protocol) is at least as safe and effective as usual care in patients with brain or nervous system injuries who are in neurological early rehabilitation and still have a tracheostomy.

The main question is:
Is the new early decannulation protocol not worse than standard care for successful tracheostomy removal by the time patients leave hospital?

If successful, the new approach could:

•     Reduce the need for intensive home nursing care after discharge

•     Improve quality of life, participation, and independence in daily activities

•     Lower costs by reducing complications and shortening rehabilitation stays.

Human participants are needed because no validated, standardized decannulation pathway exists for this patient group, and key outcomes (swallowing, breathing stability, secretion management, quality of life) cannot be studied in animals or lab models.
Study aims

 •    Primary aim: Show that the criteria‑based early decannulation protocol is not worse than standard care for successful decannulation at discharge.

•     Secondary aims: Assess effects on neurological status, quality of life, independence, swallowing, complications, long‑term outcomes (6 months), staff acceptance, feasibility, and cost‑effectiveness.
conditions: Cannulated Patients in neurological early rehabilitation

interventions.name: Patients in the intervention group undergo regular assessment for early proactive decannulation based on predefined essential criteria. Assessment of decannulation eligibility is initiated within 72 hours after study inclusion and repeated on each subsequent business day (Monday–Friday) until criter

• Patients receive standard care following baseline visit T0.
• Tracheostomy tube weaning and decannulation are performed according to current standard criteria and institutional protocols, that can differ slightly between centers.
• Monitoring and interdisciplinary therapy are conducted as usual.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Inpatient treatment at the neurological early rehabilitation center
• Acute, non-progressive neurological illnesses (e.g., stroke, traumatic brain injury (TBI), critical illness polyneuropathy/myopathy (CIP/CIM)
• Fitted with a cuffed tracheostomy tube
• Successfully weaned from mechanical ventilation > 72 h
• Acute onset of illness ≤ 8 weeks prior to enrollment
• Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) > 5
• Provision of written informed consent by the patient or legal guardian
Exclusion criteria:
• Palliative treatment or life expectancy < 12 months, according to medical assessment
• Progressive neurological disorders associated with ysphagia (e.g., ALS, Parkinson’s disease)
• Medical contraindication to decannulation (e.g., high cervical paraplegia, laryngeal/pharyngeal tumor)
• Pre-existing need for a tracheostomy tube
• Requirement for intensive care, vasopressor support, continuous sedation
• Necessity of wearing a neck brace in case of unstable cervical spine
